hypothesis: A WRITE_AND_READ_REGISTERS request can write before the register buffer when its write address is below the configured start_registers, while its read range is valid. The write-range validation repeats the read-index lower-bound check instead of checking mapping_address_write.
evidence_source: Lines 952-953 compute separate read and write mapping indices. In the bounds check at lines 962-965, mapping_address < 0 appears twice; mapping_address_write < 0 is never checked. Consequently, the assignment at line 980 can index mb_mapping->tab_registers with a negative i.
input_artifact: not_available (static source review; no input artifact)
expected_behavior: An out-of-bounds write before the register allocation, potentially producing an AddressSanitizer heap-buffer-overflow report, memory corruption, or a crash.

notes: Requires a register mapping with a nonzero start address. Valid quantity and byte-count fields do not prevent the defect. Replace the duplicate read-index lower-bound check at line 964 with a check of mapping_address_write.
